First it makes its signal strong enough that your phone thinks that the stingray is the closest/strongest tower. Your phone always tries to connect to the closest/strongest tower because you get better service that way.

The next exploit comes from the encryption level set at the tower. There are multiple levels of encryption available, but the important one to note is that no encryption is a valid level. Your phone goes along with whatever the 'tower' says and sends information back and forth at that encryption level specified by the 'tower'.

So the stingray sets the encryption level to none so that they can capture all data without having to decrypt it. And they forward all the captured packets to the real tower.

The user never knows that their cell phone is connected to a stingray instead of a real tower because the stingray doesn't modify the data, only records the data being sent through it and passes it along. Kind of like a proxy.
